newsitem.title: UK: Wm. Morrison drops after 2nd-half caution.
newsitem.headline: Wm. Morrison drops after 2nd-half caution.

text.p: Shares in William Morrison Supermarkets Plc dropped in early trading on Thursday after the company posted an eight percent rise in first-half pre-tax profit but warned sales growth would slow in the second half.
The stock was down 5-1/2p at 154-1/2 by 0740 GMT, after falling as low as 152p -- its lowest in three months.
"There is no doubt things are very difficult for the second line supermarket operators, they are finding it very tough," said one trader.
Yet analysts said it was not immediately clear to what extent the slowdown was due to competitive pressures or an extensive store refurbishment programme.
"One concern is a decline in growth in the core business but how much of that is due to the refit programme is difficult to know," said one analyst, who asked not to be named.
The analyst said the stock would likely continue to be buoyed by takeover speculation as the UK supermarket sector consolidates, yet it may find it hard to retain its premium rating if growth slows.
"It is a quality business but no more so than the others in the sector," the analyst said.

In its statement, Morrison said supermarket takings excluding petrol were 3.1 percent higher in existing stores, which was extremely encouraging when allowance was made for disruption caused by its store refurbishment programme.
"The trading conditions experienced in the period under review have been some of the most demanding for many years," the company said.
"During the second half of the year we expect trading conditions to remain difficult and sales are unlikely to maintain the growth seen in the first six months."
But it said it expected the benefits of recent investments to continue to grow and prospects remained encouraging.
The company posted a rise in pre-tax profits to 55.2 million stg in the first half from 51.1 million a year earlier and raised its dividend 18.2 percent to 0.325p.
